brief.recommendation: Waiting costs ~$134,011 in lost checkout revenue and EXCEEDS the 60s business tolerance, while terminating incurs only a 2-minute replay of the replayable price_sync workload (policy may_interrupt). Terminating the root blocker releases locks for 12 waiting checkout sessions, reducing timeouts and recovering checkout success rate toward SLO 95%.

audit.report: The batch_worker process running batch_replayable_price_sync became the root blocker for 12 checkout sessions, causing checkout success to drop to 54% with 27 timeouts in 15 seconds. After a 2-round negotiation, the guardians agreed to terminate the workload. The termination released the locks, but verification shows checkout success remains at 29% with 12 sessions still waiting on locks, indicating the blocker was only one of several contributing factors. Revenue at risk was approximately $13,493 per minute during the incident, exceeding the business tolerance of 60 seconds of degraded checkout.
audit.root_cause: batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync became an idle-in-transaction root blocker, preventing checkout sessions from acquiring locks and causing a cascade of timeouts.
lessons: Instrument batch_replayable_price_sync with a deadline or watchdog so that if it stalls >60s it can be pre-emptively terminated, avoiding the $134k revenue loss calculation that drove this negotiation.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian correctly prioritized the revenue impact analysis (BIZ-4) and moved to terminate once the trade-off favored the 2-minute replay over continued wait. The continuity guardian initially stalled the termination by citing missing invariants (biz.change_calendar, db.protected_settlements), but the probes confirmed those sets were empty, allowing R2 to pass without substantive objection.
follow_ups: Run a lock-state snapshot across all batch_worker processes to identify any other idle-in-transaction sessions that could cause future checkout timeouts.
Configure the pricing job price_sync to emit a metrics alert if its transaction duration exceeds 60s, enabling faster escalation before the $134k loss threshold is reached.

proposal.rationale: The root blocker batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync has been idle in transaction for 4.1s. Waiting allows it to complete naturally without terminating a replayable workload. The business tolerance is 60s of degraded checkout; at the current rate of timeouts (27 in 15s), the blocker is likely to finish within that window. Requesting biz.tradeoff and biz.workload_registry probes will clarify whether waiting is cheaper than interrupting.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker finishes within ~60s, the 12 waiting sessions will acquire their locks and checkout success should recover to SLO levels. If the blocker runs longer, checkout continues to degrade but no permanent action is taken.
proposal.risk_assessment: Prolonged blocker duration could push checkout degradation beyond the 60s business tolerance, increasing revenue at risk. Without registry data, we cannot be certain the blocker will finish soon.
